Open transport

Four steps from quote to driveway

Never shipped a car before? Here is what happens, in order.

Get your quote

Send us the route and vehicle details. We reply with a price and a pickup window.

We assign a carrier

We match your route to a vetted carrier and confirm the pickup date with you.

Pickup and inspection

The driver walks the vehicle with you and records its condition on the bill of lading.

Delivery and sign-off

Inspect the vehicle against the pickup report, sign, and you’re done. Note any damage before the driver leaves.

Tell us how we did

Before you book

Short, practical, and written by the people who dispatch these loads.

Get your car ready

  • Wash it so scratches show on inspection
  • Photograph all sides, roof, and odometer
  • Leave about a quarter tank of fuel
  • Remove toll tags and loose accessories
  • Hand over one key, disable the alarm

Spot a lowball quote

  • A quote far under everyone else is bait
  • A big deposit before a carrier is assigned
  • No MC or DOT number you can look up
  • Won’t name the carrier once dispatched
  • Different person every time you call

Time your shipment

  • A flexible pickup date can lower the price
  • Summer and holidays are busier, so book early
  • Rural pickups take longer than interstate ones
  • Tell us up front if the vehicle doesn’t run

Answers before you commit

Short answers before you book.

How much does it cost to ship a car?

Distance, vehicle size, whether it runs, and open versus enclosed carrier. Per-mile rates fall as distance rises. Use the price tool above for an estimate, and your dispatcher confirms the final number.

When do I pay, and how?

Your dispatcher explains payment terms when you book, including what is due and when. Ask for them in writing.

How long will it take?

Your dispatcher gives you a pickup window before you book. Transit is roughly 1 to 3 days under 500 miles and several days coast to coast. Weather and driver hours can move it.

Is my vehicle insured during transport?

Carriers are insured up to $1.5 million, and we check coverage before assigning your vehicle. We also carry a broker bond for added safety. Personal items are not covered.

Can I leave items in the car?

Keep it light and keep valuables with you. Personal items are generally not covered by cargo insurance, and some carriers refuse them.

Can you ship a vehicle that doesn’t run?

Yes, with a winch-equipped carrier. It should still roll, brake, and steer. Tell us up front so we assign the right equipment.

Can you move larger trucks?

Yes. Pickups, dually trucks, box trucks, and other oversize vehicles. Include the size and weight in your request.

Do you pick up from auctions?

Yes. Send the lot number, buyer ID, and gate pass details when you book. Book the same day you win the lot to limit storage fees.

What if my vehicle is damaged in transit?

Note it on the bill of lading before the driver leaves, take photos, and contact us the same day. A signed clean receipt makes claims very hard to win.

Can I track my vehicle?

Once dispatched, you get the carrier’s contact and your dispatcher can give you the carrier’s latest location.
